title: A Night at the Museum with Moths: An Entomological Collaboration for the Public
content: Across the globe, people are captivated by insects. In cities, the insects most often commonly recognized are either pests—the sight of which can be so terrible that some people just cannot look away—or key beneficial insects that are beloved by the public in urban settings (Polák et al. 2020, Fukano and Soga 2021). Regardless of the reason for the fascination, insects get people’s attention. When people are fascinated by insects, this makes for an excellent outreach scenario in which entomologists can teach the public about entomology, which reinforces the mutual trust that communities have in science and which may lead to an eventual change in cultural attitudes and policy decisions (Ben-Zvi 2024).
